title: StochasticConstrainedQuasar.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Objectives may be nonconvex; only quasar-convexity and L-Lipschitz gradients on X are required.

problem_class.label: quasar
problem_class.details: On X, γ(f(x)−f(xstar)) ≤ ⟨∇f(x),x−xstar⟩, where 0<γ≤1 and xstar minimizes f over X.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns g(x,ω), with IID seeds, E[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x) and E‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ² for x∈X. No function-value oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticConstrainedQuasar.lean: spec.admissible, oracle answer and moment conditions; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the exact Euclidean projection onto X, characterized by ⟨z−proj(z),w−proj(z)⟩≤0 for every w∈X. Projection calls have a separate fixed budget.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: σ≥0 bounds the centered second moment uniformly on X. No exponential-tail or almost-sure noise bound is assumed; finite-variance heavy-tailed noise is permitted.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: X is compact and convex, has diameter at most D>0, and contains x0 and xstar. Smoothness is required only on X; ∇f(xstar)=0 is not required. L,D,γ,σ,ε,δ and x0 are public; f,X,xstar and the sampling law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticConstrainedQuasar.lean: Params, Instance, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output must satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: Output membership in X is required jointly with the objective-gap guarantee.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The probability of failing either feasibility or ε objective accuracy is at most δ∈(0,1), under the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, with fixed per-oracle budgets.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Combines constrained quasar-convex optimization with projection access and high-probability objective accuracy under only finite-variance stochastic gradients.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Constrained Quasar Minimization

We consider minimizing f:E→R over a compact convex set X in a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E. On X, the function has an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0, and is γ-quasar-convex relative to a minimizer x⋆∈X, where 0<γ≤1. The oracles return unbiased stochastic gradients with bounded variance using independent, identically distributed samples, and exact Euclidean projections onto X. Given ε>0 and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying both x¯∈X and f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ over sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Xf(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, a starting point x0, and the parameters L,D>0, γ∈(0,1], σ≥0, ε>0, and δ∈(0,1); the objective, feasible set, minimizer, and sampling distribution are accessed through the oracles.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible geometry). The set X⊆E is compact and convex, contains x0 and x⋆, and satisfies ∥x−y∥≤D,x,y∈X.

Assumption 2 (Smoothness and quasar convexity). The function f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of X, and, for every x,y∈X, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,f(x⋆)≤f(x),γ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient oracle). There are a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈X, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼ν, with Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2. The oracle uses a sequence (ξk)k≥0 of measurable, mutually independent sample variables, each with law ν, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. At a stochastic gradient call with query x, it returns g(x,ξk) using the sample at that call’s index.

Assumption 4 (Exact projection oracle). The projection oracle returns ΠX(z) at z∈E, where ΠX(z)∈X,⟨z−ΠX(z),w−ΠX(z)⟩≤0,w∈X.

Both oracles accept queries throughout E; the gradient and moment conditions above apply on X. Stochastic gradient calls and projection calls have separate budgets. After these calls, the output x¯∈E must be measurable and satisfy P{x¯∉X or f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε}≤δ, where P is the joint law of the samples and the independent algorithm randomness.

comparisonHtml:
A finite-dimensional real Hilbert space; compact convex X of diameter at most D>0, with x0,x⋆∈X and x⋆∈arg⁡minXf. The differentiable objective has L-Lipschitz gradient on X, L>0, and γ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩ for x∈X, 0<γ≤1. Access: exact projection and jointly measurable IID stochastic gradients, with ∫g(x,ω)dp=∇f(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−∇f(x)∥2dp≤σ2. Target: P{x^∈X, f(x^)−f(x⋆)≤ε}≥1−δ, ε>0, 0<δ<1.

Matches deterministic polynomial rate at σ=0. (1): At σ=0, pays h and gives probability 1−δ rather than certainty.
(3) QASGD (Fu et al. 2023), Cor. 3.3 O([1+RL/ε+σ2R2γ2ε2]ℓR(ε)) component value/gradient calls; expected gap. Unconstrained; L-smooth components, bounded gradient second moment. (1): Scope: constrained boundary minimizers; variance instead of gradient-second-moment bound. Oracle: no component values. High-confidence guarantee. (1): Needs compact X, known D; D replaces R, potentially costly for R≪D.
(4) Derived bound: (Fu et al. 2023), Cor. 3.3 + Markov O([1+RL/(εδ)+σ2R2γ2ε2δ2]ℓR(εδ)) component value/gradient calls; confidence 1−δ. Restrictions of (3). (1): On overlap with R≍D, noise-term confidence dependence becomes hℓ2 instead of δ−2ℓR(εδ); improves when the latter dominates. (1): Requires a known compact feasible set containing a global minimizer; D may greatly exceed R.

Abbr: h=1+log⁡(1/δ); ℓ=1+log⁡(2+LD2/(γ2ε)); ℓR(a)=1+log⁡(1+LR2/(γa)); R bounds initial distance to a global minimizer. In (3), (4), σ2 bounds the stochastic gradient’s second moment. p is the sample law and P the IID sequence law. Costs include search and inner-solve calls.

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticConstrainedQuasar

open OracleTemplate

structure Params extends SmoothAndConvex.Public.{0} where
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  D : ℝ
  γ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.finiteE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

structure Instance (q : Params) where
  f : q.E → ℝ
  X : Set q.E
  xstar : q.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.D ∧ 0 < q.γ ∧ q.γ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧
    0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ < 1
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)) (proj : q.E → q.E),
    StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k)
      (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (i, x) seed => if i = 0 then g x seed else proj x } ∧
    (∀ z, proj z ∈ I.X ∧ ∀ w ∈ I.X, ⟪z - proj z, w - proj z⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    IsCompact I.X ∧ Convex ℝ I.X ∧ q.x0 ∈ I.X ∧ I.xstar ∈ I.X ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, ∀ y ∈ I.X, ‖x - y‖ ≤ q.D) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, ∀ y ∈ I.X, ‖gradient I.f x - gradient I.f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    IsMinOn I.f I.X I.xstar ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, q.γ * (I.f x - I.f I.xstar) ≤ ⟪gradient I.f x, x - I.xstar⟫) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, Integrable (g x) (p : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, (∫ ω, g x ω ∂(p : Measure _)) = gradient I.f x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2) (p : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.X, (∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(p : Measure _)) ≤ q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      (P : Measure _) {ω | ¬(output ω ∈ I.X ∧ I.f (output ω) - I.f I.xstar ≤ q.ε)} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal q.δ

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticConstrainedQuasar
